question:
All of the triangles in the diagram below are similar to isosceles triangle \(ABC,\) in which \(AB=AC.\) Each of the \(7\) smallest triangles has area \(1,\) and \(\triangle ABC\) has area \(40.\) What is the area of trapezoid \(DBCE?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2018_AMC_10A_Q09_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The seven unit-area triangles determine the relative sizes of the two triangles above their strip.

Let \(F\) and \(G\) be the endpoints of the upper segment, with \(F\) on \(AB\) and \(G\) on \(AC\). Triangles \(AFG\) and \(ADE\) are similar to \(ABC\) and share its angle at \(A\). Their equal sides therefore meet at \(A\), and their base angles equal those of \(ABC\). These equal angles show that \(FG\), \(DE\), and \(BC\) are parallel.

Let \(h>0\) be the perpendicular distance between \(FG\) and \(DE\). Each of the seven smallest triangles has its base on one of these lines and height \(h\). Because each has area \(1\), every such base has the same length
\[
b=\frac{2}{h}.
\]
The upper boundary \(FG\) contains three of these bases, while \(DE\) contains four. Hence
\[
\frac{FG}{DE}=\frac{3b}{4b}=\frac34.
\]
For similar triangles, both base and height scale by the same factor, so area scales by its square. Thus the area of \(AFG\) is \(9/16\) of the area of \(ADE\).

Let \(X\) be the area of \(ADE\). The seven small triangles fill the strip between \(FG\) and \(DE\) without overlap, so
\[
X-\frac{9}{16}X=7,
\qquad \frac{7}{16}X=7,
\qquad X=16.
\]
Removing \(ADE\) from \(ABC\) leaves trapezoid \(DBCE\). Its area is therefore
\[
40-16=\boxed{24},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
